the role of intragroup treatment for the formation of collective identity and willingness to engage into group-serving behavior.

respectful intragroup behavior is beneficial for group functioning, but not always and not necessarily.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
respect for fellow group members, as expressed by fellow group members, is an important determinant of collective identification and group-serving behavior.
intragroup respect is a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for collective identification and willingness-to-serve the group.
intragroup respect, as defined in this study, is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the emergence of collective identification and group-serving behavior in groups.

respect for group members, irrespective of the performance evaluation, is an important prerequisite of a positive group climate.
intragroup respect is a key factor of group identification and group-serving behavior.
